title: Changing the transform of a collision node in a process will always interpolate it (even with interpolation off)
body: ### Tested versions - Reproducible in: v4.7.2.stable.official [ed1daf0bf] ### System information Godot v4.7.2.stable - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4050 Laptop GPU (NVIDIA; 32.0.16.1060) - 13th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-13650HX (20 threads) - 15.69 GiB memory - WASAPI (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono) ### Issue description Even with physics interpolation off, collision nodes seem to run calculations with interpolated transforms if you change the transform outside of a physics process. I found this easiest to observe with the mouse entered/exited functions. The MRP project has two collision shapes on top of each other with the exact same shape. When the mouse is touching it, it swaps the collision shapes by setting their scale (0 for disabled, 1 for enabled). However, the mouse entered and exited signals rapidly fire near the edge of the shape due to the shapes interpolating their scale, which cannot be visually seen. ### Steps to reproduce Observe a result of unwanted interpolation: - Open the MRP project - Make sure "visible collision shapes" is turned on - Run the scene and move the mouse into the outer edge of the collision shape - You should see that it rapidly flickers between "true" and "false" - Move the mouse close to the center of the collision shape, and the flickering stops Why the flickering is explained by interpolation: - Go to project settings and enable physics/common/physics_interpolation - Now when trying the example again, you can visually see the shapes interpolating. It matches up with the flickering seen with interpolation off. How to fix the flickering: - Switch the process function for a physics process ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [mouse-collision-bug.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33641413/mouse-collision-bug.zip)
